South Africa has narrowly avoided what investigators describe as a potential national security breach following revelations that controversial businessman and accused criminal Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala allegedly pursued plans to establish a luxury private terminal at OR Tambo International Airport.

According to investigative reports by News24 and Eyewitness News, the proposal, known as the “Green Lounge,” had reached an advanced planning stage and envisioned a fully functioning private terminal that would allow selected clients to fast-track immigration and customs processes. 

The plan raised alarm because it would have placed security screening at a national key point in the hands of Matlala’s private agents.

The scheme reportedly included a R70 million-a-year funding pitch to Nedbank, framed as an exclusive service for ultra-wealthy clients.

However, concerns intensified due to Matlala’s criminal profile and alleged links to drug cartels, prompting warnings that the project could have compromised border control and national security. 

Matlala is currently detained in a super maximum security prison in Kokstad and faces multiple serious charges, including attempted murder, fraud, and conspiracy to commit murder. 

The revelations have reignited debate over governance, oversight, and how individuals with serious criminal allegations can gain proximity to critical state infrastructure.".

Alleged ‘green lounge’ plan by Cat Matlala at OR Tambo sparks national security fears  
  
South Africa has narrowly avoided what investigators describe as a potential national security breach following revelations that controversial businessman and accused criminal Vusimuzi “Cat” Matlala allegedly pursued plans to establish a luxury private terminal at OR Tambo International Airport.  
  
According to investigative reports by News24 and Eyewitness News, the proposal, known as the “Green Lounge,” had reached an advanced planning stage and envisioned a fully functioning private terminal that would allow selected clients to fast-track immigration and customs processes.  
  
The plan raised alarm because it would have placed security screening at a national key point in the hands of Matlala’s private agents.  
  
The scheme reportedly included a R70 million-a-year funding pitch to Nedbank, framed as an exclusive service for ultra-wealthy clients.  
  
However, concerns intensified due to Matlala’s criminal profile and alleged links to drug cartels, prompting warnings that the project could have compromised border control and national security.  
  
Matlala is currently detained in a super maximum security prison in Kokstad and faces multiple serious charges, including attempted murder, fraud, and conspiracy to commit murder.  
  
The revelations have reignited debate over governance, oversight, and how individuals with serious criminal allegations can gain proximity to critical state infrastructure.

Suspended SAPS Organised Crime Unit Member Sergeant Fannie Nkosi To Face More Criminal Charges In Limpopo
Suspended South African Police Service (SAPS) Organised Crime Unit member Sergeant Fannie Nkosi's woes are far from over.
This comes after the Madlanga Commission’s Recommendations Investigative Task Team brought additional charges of defeating and obstructing the course of justice against him.
According to SAPS National Spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe, Nkosi is now expected to appear before the Thohoyandou Magistrate’s Court on Friday.
"It is alleged that on 10 November 2022, a suspect was arrested for possession of dagga, unlicensed firearms, and explosives. Investigations indicate that Nkosi fetched the original case docket under the pretext that he had been sent by Head Office. A few months later, he allegedly returned to Thohoyandou, identified himself as a colonel from Head Office, and removed the confiscated dagga from police custody," she said.
Mathe said Nkosi later booked the exhibit in at Head Office, but it was subsequently discovered that one of the exhibit bags containing the dagga had been tampered with."A case of defeating and obstructing the course of justice has been registered for investigation," she said.
Nkosi is currently in custody after he was denied bail in April.
He is a focal figure in a massive, high-level police corruption scandal exposed during his extensive testimony at the Madlanga Commission.Following his eight-day testimony at the Madlanga Commission, a specialised task team raided Nkosi's Pretoria North home.
The raid uncovered severe breaches of law enforcement protocols, resulting in his immediate arrest. 
He faces a sheet of criminal charges, including theft and money laundering, after he was found with over R50,000 in cash hidden under a mattress without explanation.
He was also found keeping six official SAPS case dockets at his house while under suspension.
